summary: Lunar Mission Builder is an interactive web application that uses NASA data, mathematical models and 3D visualizations to analyze lunar landing sites and plan missions from Earth to the Moon. It addresses the challenge by combining landing site selection, solar illumination analysis, communication availability and launch planning into a single platform. The project simplifies complex scientific calculations, making preliminary lunar mission planning more efficient, accessible and understandable for researchers, engineers and students.
details:
Lunar Mission Builder provides a structured approach to lunar mission planning from defining mission requirements to selecting a landing site, launch vehicle and flight trajectory. The system processes scientific data to calculate environmental conditions and evaluate possible mission scenarios.

Users can examine how landing dates and locations affect sunlight, communication windows and surface conditions. The platform presents these results through visual models, timelines and comparisons, helping identify suitable mission options and understand their limitations.

The project is intended to support preliminary mission analysis and education. It provides an accessible environment for exploring lunar mission scenarios, understanding engineering challenges and studying the factors that influence mission feasibility.

The application uses Python, Flask, NumPy and Skyfield for scientific calculations and data processing. JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Three.js and WebGL support the interactive interface and 3D visualizations. Docker, GitHub and automated testing tools are used for development and deployment.

A distinctive feature is the integration of separate mission-planning stages into a connected workflow. Changes in landing locations, mission dates or technical requirements can be explored across different modules, making relationships between mission parameters easier to understand.

The development prioritizes calculation accuracy, data reliability and realistic engineering constraints. Particular attention is given to lunar terrain, solar illumination, Earth visibility, temperature, radiation, launch limitations and mission risks. Scientific calculations are validated against reference data while the interface is designed to remain clear and responsive.
